title: Table S1. Deviations D1-D12 (post hoc, exploratory)
content: L1 RA linear scores use this primary rule. In the gene log2 matrix of the 285 analysed samples, drop a gene from every sample when more than 50 percent of its values are non-finite, and treat that gene as absent. Fill the remaining non-finite values with impute::impute.knn from impute 1.84.0, k = 10, and the other arguments at their defaults, then score. Sensitivity: a complete-case score that drops every gene with any non-finite value.
reason: Recorded before any family-P result was seen. A sample-specific gene drop would make the omitted genes part of the within-person variation. Complete-case retention leaves 13 of 214 RA_default genes. kNN is the missing-value method inside RNAAgeCalc.

title: Table S1. Deviations D1-D12 (post hoc, exploratory)
content: For H2, H3, H4, H5, S4, and every sensitivity, a sample with a non-finite model input, score or covariate, is dropped from that model only. The run does not stop for this reason. Each drop is written to results/confirm/exclusions_runtime.tsv with step, dataset, clock, sample, and reason. Any other error follows instruction 7 section 3.4.

title: Table S1. Deviations D1-D12 (post hoc, exploratory)
content: L1 missing values have an additional sensitivity, participant-mean imputation. For each participant and gene, a missing value is filled with the mean of that participant's observed values of the same gene. If that participant has no observed value, the value is filled with the mean of the gene across all analysed samples. Filled values are constant within a participant and add no within-person time variation. RA linear scores and TAms and module scores are recomputed on this matrix by the frozen scoring path, and model M is fit as in the L1 family-P tests. The primary analysis stays D1 for RA and the frozen code for TAms.
reason: H2 이후 결과 보기 전. kNN can copy circadian variation from co-expressed genes into the filled values. The frozen TAms path keeps only genes that are finite in every sample, 1154 of 19541 on L1. Participant-mean imputation is the opposite direction.
